The work of postsecondary criminal justice and law enforcement teachers can be divided into three connected but independent work areas. The first is teaching and course design: write or revise course syllabi and teaching materials against the curriculum goals, prepare and teach courses such as criminal law and law enforcement and investigative techniques and corrections and judicial administration, lead classroom discussions and organize case and simulation exercises, assign and grade homework and papers and exams and register grades, and maintain attendance and teaching files as the school requires. The second is academic research and writing: keep tracking new developments in the criminal
justice and law enforcement field, read literature and discuss with peers and attend professional conferences, conduct research in a specific area and write and publish results in professional journals or monographs, compile references and reading materials, write grant proposals to seek external research funding, and possibly provide professional consulting to government departments or the industry. The third is student guidance and institutional collaboration: receive students at fixed times, guide academic and career development and write recommendation letters, supervise student internships and teaching assistantships and research work, take part in
student recruitment and employment referral, serve on committees handling institutional policy and departmental affairs, and possibly hold administrative roles such as department chair or serve as a student club advisor. The three work areas alternate, but their basis and responsibility and assessment differ; research universities and teaching institutions and community colleges and police training institutions also place different emphasis. 
The three work areas are an editorial organization, and research publication and grant applications and internship research supervision and clubs are Supplemental, so actual involvement varies and is not a fixed process for every teacher.

Core purpose

Teach learners the knowledge and methods of criminal justice and corrections and law enforcement administration, and advance the field's understanding through research and writing: ensure the course content is accurate and evaluation is consistent and guidance is followable and academic results are reviewable.

Core purposes of adjacent positions: institutional administrators handle student affairs and academic affairs and institutional operations; other subject teachers teach their own discipline's courses; law teachers develop legal professional ability; social work teachers develop social service and clinical practice ability; correctional officers and bailiffs carry out custody and security duties in detention facilities.
Main object and basis

Learners and courses and teaching materials and student records, as well as the research questions and literature in the criminal justice and law enforcement field; the basis is the curriculum plan and teaching standards and academic integrity and evaluation criteria and student record and privacy management requirements.

Objects and bases of adjacent positions: student affairs and academic affairs processes (administrators), the discipline's knowledge system (other subject teachers), legal norms and legal practice (law teachers), social service and clinical practice standards (social work teachers), and detainee management and detention security rules (correctional officers and bailiffs).
Core process

Write the syllabus and materials → prepare classes → teach and lead discussion → assign and grade → register grades → guide and archive; research advances separately through proposing questions and conducting research and writing and publishing.

Processes of adjacent positions: policy execution and student services (administrators), teaching and research in the discipline (other subject teachers), legal courses and practice training (law teachers), social work courses and internship supervision (social work teachers), and custody patrols and security handling (correctional officers and bailiffs).
Main outputs

Course syllabi and teaching materials, lecturing and discussion, grading and grade records, guidance records, academic papers and research reports, and internship and teaching assistant supervision records.

Outputs of adjacent positions: institutional policy and student service records (administrators), the discipline's course and research results (other subject teachers), legal course and practice training results (law teachers), social work course and supervision records (social work teachers), and custody and security handling records (correctional officers and bailiffs).
Responsible party

Teachers in this occupation are responsible for the accuracy of course content and the consistency of evaluation and the truthfulness and completeness of grade registration and student records; whether a course can be offered and academic titles and appointments and funding and research direction must be handled per institutional policy and academic procedure and are not decided unilaterally.

Responsible parties of adjacent positions: institutional managers are responsible for institutional operations and student affairs; other subject teachers are responsible for teaching and scholarship in their discipline; law teachers are responsible for legal courses and practice training; social work teachers are responsible for social work courses and internship supervision; correctional officers and bailiffs are responsible for custody and security in detention facilities.
Collaboration and supervision

Submit and review with department colleagues and the teaching committee and academic affairs and academic administration per authority; coordinate supervision with internship and partner units; on a course content dispute or an academic integrity issue or a student record risk or a conflict of interest, verify and report and keep records per the actual matter and role authority and institutional procedure. An ordinary dispute does not automatically authorize a full suspension or resumption of teaching.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: institutional managers collaborate with teachers and administrative departments; other subject teachers collaborate with department colleagues; law teachers collaborate with the law school and legal practice institutions; social work teachers collaborate with social service institutions; correctional officers and bailiffs collaborate with detention management and judicial departments.

values: Hypothetical teaching and research scenario material (practice input)

Hypothetical situation: a postsecondary criminal justice and law enforcement teacher receives a hypothetical teaching and research task and encounters four problems. First, one statement about law enforcement procedure in the syllabus is inconsistent with the statement in the designated textbook, and a student has already raised the question in class; second, a student's final paper is highly similar to other sources, and the student says they only referenced the material; third, someone in the course group asks for the previous semester's grade ranking to be published, and another student asks to see another person's grades individually; fourth, an institution
invites the teacher to provide paid consulting for a law enforcement training program whose content relates to their ongoing research project.

Given materials: the course syllabus and teaching materials; the textbook and reference list; the student paper and the similarity check result; the institution's policy on academic integrity and grade management and student information protection; and the training invitation letter.

Materials not given: the discretion rule for which prevails when the syllabus and textbook statements conflict, the specific threshold at which similarity counts as academic misconduct, the specific provisions on the shareable scope of student information, and the discretion rule for whether outside consulting requires declaration and how to recuse. If the practice needs these conditions, state clearly your assumptions and the party you need to confirm them with.
Task requirements

Please write a one-page handling and communication plan: including the verification and explanation of the course statement conflict, the handling of the paper similarity suspicion and the academic integrity procedure, the compliant response to the grade and information sharing requests, and the declaration and recusal arrangement for the outside consulting invitation.

The plan must state which information comes from the prompt material and which is still an assumption, and explain whether it relies on the syllabus and textbook or the institutional policy statement or the training invitation letter.
Reference deliverables (derivable from the prompt)

The plan should include: the course statement conflict (list both statements and explain the difference, determine the handling path per the curriculum goals and the institutional course approval procedure, tell students before confirmation that it will be verified per procedure, and do not choose one side on your own), the paper similarity suspicion (retain the original material and the similarity check result, submit it under the institutional academic integrity procedure and have the corresponding body determine it, do not make a disciplinary decision yourself, and do not publicly discuss the student's case before a conclusion), grades and information sharing (explain that grade ranking and other people's grades are student personal
information, handle it per institutional policy and the minimum necessity principle, do not disclose another person's information because of a group request, and give an executable application channel), outside consulting (declare per institutional policy and explain the relationship with the ongoing project, recuse or adjust the scope where necessary, and handle matters involving sensitive information per procedure), and handover (state clearly the status of the four matters and the actions taken and the to-be-confirmed items).
The reference deliverables list only the elements that should be included and do not require wording identical to the example; being able to explain the judgment basis is enough.

subject.summary:
In the United States, postsecondary criminal justice and law enforcement teachers correspond to O*NET-SOC 25-1111.00 (Criminal Justice and Law Enforcement Teachers, Postsecondary), teaching criminal justice and corrections and law enforcement administration courses in higher education institutions and police and judicial training institutions, including both teachers focused on teaching and those balancing teaching and research: prepare and
teach courses such as criminal law and law enforcement and investigative techniques, lead classroom discussions, grade homework and papers and exams and register grades, write and revise course syllabi and teaching materials, receive students at fixed times and guide their academic and career development, collaborate with colleagues on teaching and research topics, take part in student recruitment and employment referral, write academic results and take part in professional associations and institutional affairs, supervise student internships and research, and possibly hold an administrative role or provide professional consulting externally. The preparation level for this occupation is 
Job Zone Five (most require a graduate degree), and similar positions on the China side are university teachers and police instructors, whose appointment and evaluation bases are not a one-to-one correspondence with that US occupation segment and cannot be interchanged.
